extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants/practitioners in biotechnology (deposit and sequence disclosures)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for compliance with USPTO rules on deposits of biological material and the preparation/submission of nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings (WIPO ST.25/ST.26 and 37 CFR provisions) in patent applications. Covers when deposits are required, acceptable depositories, timing, viability/furnishing, and detailed file/format/content rules for sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit Rules (37 CFR 1.801-1.809)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules setting forth examining procedures and conditions of deposit which must be satisfied when a deposit of biological material is required for patent purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These regulations address procedural matters for deposits of biological materials for patents (do not decide substantive necessity); deposits facilitate satisfaction of 35 U.S.C. 112 enablement/written description/best mode issues; see PCT Rule 13bis and related MPEP sections for international rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material Capable of Self-Replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological material for deposit includes material that is capable of self-replication either directly or indirectly (examples: bacteria, fungi including yeast, algae, protozoa, eukaryotic cells, cell lines, hybridomas, plasmids, viruses, plant tissue cells, lichens and seeds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect self-replication includes material that replicates only when another self-replicating biological material is present (e.g., replication after insertion in a host). Viruses, phages, plasmids, replication-defective cells are examples of indirect replicating material. Deposits of host cells may be used to reproduce non-living materials (e.g., vectors).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a Deposit May be Needed (37 CFR 1.802)
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit is necessary only where access to the biological material is required to satisfy the statutory requirements for patentability under 35 U.S.C. 112 (enablement, written description, best mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to a deposit may be included even if not required. Examiners should not require a deposit where the applicant shows that deposit of starting material or other information suffices for enablement without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological Material Known and Readily Available
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid deposit, the biological material must be both 'known' and 'readily available' to the public; neither concept alone is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors indicating known and readily available include commercial availability, printed references, declarations by those in the field, predictable isolation techniques, or an existing compliant deposit. The Office will accept clear and convincing evidence of public access, but the applicant assumes the risk if the material later ceases to be accessible. The Office can certify availability only under conditions (see 37 CFR 1.808(c) criteria A–D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological Material That Can Be Made or Isolated Without Undue Experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit is not required if the required biological materials can be made or isolated without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits may be required where an isolation procedure requires undue experimentation. If materials can be obtained from publicly available material with only routine experimentation and a reliable screening test, no deposit is required (cited cases: Tabuchi v. Nubel; Ex Parte Hata).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to a Deposit in the Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere reference to a biological material in the specification or the actual deposit does not create a presumption that the deposit was necessary to satisfy 35 U.S.C. 112 or that deposit under the regulations was required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reference present in the application upon filing can form the basis for making a deposit later (if required), but adding such a reference after filing risks introducing new matter (35 U.S.C. 132).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable Depository (37 CFR 1.803)
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit is recognized if made in (1) any International Depositary Authority (IDA) under the Budapest Treaty, or (2) any other depository recognized as suitable by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitability is judged on administrative/technical competence and agreement to comply with deposit terms. The depository must: (i) have continuous existence; (ii) be independent of depositor control; (iii) possess staff/facilities to examine viability and store uncontaminated; (iv) provide safety measures to minimize loss; (v) be impartial and objective; (vi) furnish samples expeditiously; (vii) promptly notify depositors if unable to furnish samples and explain reasons. Organizations seeking recognition must provide detailed information including fees and intended scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of Making an Original Deposit (37 CFR 1.804)
rubrics_metrics.description: An original deposit may be made any time before filing the application or, subject to 37 CFR 1.809, during pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deposit is made after the effective filing date, applicant must promptly submit a corroborating statement that the deposited material is specifically identified in the application as filed. When a necessary deposit is made during pendency, it must be no later than the time set by the examiner at the Notice of Allowance and Issue Fee Due; a deposit need not be made until the application is in condition for allowance if the applicant provides a written assurance that an acceptable deposit will be made on or before payment of the issue fee, with sufficient detail to convince the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement or Supplement of Deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures exist for replacement or supplementation of a deposit in a pending application or after a patent has issued, and rules for failure to replace or exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement made after issuance or in pending cases may not always be recognized; failure to replace or improperly handled replacements can result in loss of deposit availability or other negative consequences. Specific timing, treatment, and possible exemptions are set out in the regulations (see MPEP §2406 et seq.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of Deposit and Viability; Furnishing of Samples; Conditions of Deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits must be maintained viable and accessible for specified minimum terms and under specified conditions; furnishing of samples must be possible under the depository's procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term of deposit: at least 30 years and at least 5 years after the most recent request (37 CFR 1.806). A compliant deposit will be considered readily available even if access is subject to health/safety/regulatory conditions. Depository must ensure viability, uncontaminated storage, safety measures, and timely furnishing of samples or notification of inability to furnish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of Availability of Deposit (37 CFR 1.808/1.808(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will, upon request, certify whether a deposit has been made under conditions making it available to the public as of the issue date, but only if specific criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not certify unless: (A) deposit was necessary to overcome a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112; (B) the record contains an examiner statement that a rejection would have been made 'but for' the deposit; (C) the record clearly indicates the deposit was made under the Budapest Treaty and all depositor-imposed restrictions will be irrevocably removed upon grant (with possible exception of request format per 37 CFR 1.808(b)); or (D) the record indicates an acceptable non-Budapest deposit with irrevocable removal of restrictions. If deposit not made under conditions of 1.808(a), it cannot be relied upon by third parties to establish 'known' and 'readily available' status in other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Procedures and Rejections Based on Deposit Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners follow procedures for determining whether a deposit is required and may issue rejections or request deposits when access to biological material is necessary for enablement/written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are cautioned not to require specific deposits when alternative disclosures allow enablement. Where deposit is required, examiner may set time for deposit (e.g., before issue) and must state issues clearly so applicants can respond. Replies to deposit-based rejections and related prosecution guidance are provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application in Condition for Allowance Except for Deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be otherwise allowable except for outstanding deposit requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can provide a written assurance that an acceptable deposit will be made on or before payment of the issue fee; examiner may allow conditional allowance pending deposit compliance but must be satisfied by the assurance and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of Application with Respect to Deposited Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that reference or include deposited material must include appropriate content in the specification identifying the deposit and providing necessary corroborating information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content expectations include sufficient identification of the deposited material, statements regarding the deposit, accession numbers, and other information enabling correlation between the application and the deposit; if deposit made after filing, corroborating statements are required. See MPEP for form paragraphs and sample statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Sequence Listing XML for Sequence Disclosures (WIPO ST.26 / 37 CFR 1.831-1.835)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications having nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence disclosures as defined in 37 CFR 1.831(b) (applicable to filings on/after July 1, 2022), a Sequence Listing must be provided in the 'Sequence Listing XML' format conforming to WIPO ST.26 and 37 CFR 1.831-1.835.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP provides an overview, definitions, and detailed requirements for the Sequence Listing XML; failure to submit a compliant Sequence Listing XML triggers notification procedures and may require amendment under 37 CFR 1.835. Translation of a Sequence Listing XML is not treated as an amended Sequence Listing XML. International PCT submissions to be searched/examined by the US ISA/IPEA have additional notification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML: File and Encoding Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sequence Listing XML' must be a single file encoded using Unicode UTF-8, valid according to the DTD, and must contain an XML declaration, a DOCTYPE declaration, and a root element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The XML must contain a General Information part and a Sequence Data part. Language-dependent free text qualifier values must be in English. Title element and other standardized elements must be present. The file form/format and submission method requirements (including incorporation by reference rules) are specified in the MPEP and 37 CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Representation: Symbols, Included/Excluded Residues, Modified Residues
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings must use standardized representation and symbols for nucleotide and amino acid sequences; definitions for 'amino acid', 'modified amino acid', 'nucleotide', and 'modified nucleotide' guide inclusions and exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuation should not be used to indicate unknown bases/residues or to delimit functional regions; such features should be noted in the Feature section (Appendix G numeric identifiers <220>-<223>). Presence of unnatural amino acids does not necessarily exempt a sequence from the rules. Cyclic/branched peptides rules and other special situations are discussed in MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Sequentially Numbered Sequence Identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences disclosed in the description, drawings or claims should be denoted using sequentially numbered sequence identifiers in the Sequence Listing XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent identifiers across the XML and application text/drawings/claims to allow cross-referencing. Exclusive conformance requires amendments to align embedded sequence information in text/drawings/claims with any amendment to the Sequence Listing XML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive Conformance Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive conformance requires that any amendment of the sequence information in a 'Sequence Listing' be accompanied by an amendment of corresponding information, if any, embedded in the text of the specification or presented in a drawing figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sequences are amended in the Sequence Listing XML, applicants must also amend any in-text or figure-presented sequence information to avoid inconsistencies and to prevent improper introduction of new matter. This applies to both ST.26 XML and legacy formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of Variants and Variable-Length Regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Variable-length regions and variants in sequences must still comply with the Sequence Rules; variable-length regions should be represented by repeating the variable region to the maximum length and specifying in the Features section that specified positions may be absent or present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use repeated residues up to maximum (e.g., (Xaa)n represented as Xaa repeated to max) and include a Feature (<220>-<223>) explaining that positions can be absent/present. Mandatory Features must cover every 'n' or 'Xaa' using <220> (blank), <221> (type), <222> (location), <223> (what the variable can be). When all variables are equal, ranges for <222> can cover multiple variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited Characters, Formatting and Abbreviations in Sequence Listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence Listing files have strict character and formatting rules: remove non-ASCII characters from .txt files (e.g., spell out symbols like 'alpha'), do not use tabs, do not use punctuation to indicate unknown residues, do not use single-letter amino acid abbreviations in the Sequence Listing, do not use subscripts/superscripts, and '0' is not used for negative numbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized abbreviations only (per WIPO ST.25 or well-known terms). Avoid application-specific abbreviations that are not generally understood. Failure to follow these rules may lead to error reports; applicants must correct all similar errors in the file, not just those listed in the error report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Numeric Identifiers and Field Content (<130>, <140>, <160>, <212>, <213>, <220>-<223>)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain numeric identifier fields in sequence listings are mandatory or constrained: <130> File Reference is mandatory if <140> current application number not present; <160> total number of sequences must be updated after additions/deletions; <213> can only be 'Scientific name', 'Unknown', or 'Artificial Sequence'; <212> molecule type must be consistent with feature descriptions; <220>-<223> feature fields are mandatory to explain 'n' or 'Xaa' variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Genus/species for <213> (no common names). If <213> is 'Unknown' or 'Artificial sequence', include a mandatory feature to explain the source in <223>. Ensure consistency between molecule type (<212>) and Feature descriptions; numeric identifiers and totals must be kept accurate when modifying sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments, Notifications, and Consequences for Sequence Listing Files (37 CFR 1.835 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures exist for issuance of notices for failure to comply with Sequence Listing requirements and for amendments to add an initial Sequence Listing XML or to add/delete/replace sequence information under 37 CFR 1.835.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office issues notifications for failure to submit a Sequence Listing XML for international applications to be searched/examined by the US ISA/IPEA. An amendment adding a Sequence Listing XML may be allowed under specified rules; adding translations is not treated as an amended Sequence Listing XML. Applicants must follow the regulatory amendment paths and heed presumptions regarding compliance. See MPEP §§2414–2419 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability Dates and Determining if a Sequence Listing Must Be Submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability of ST.26/XML and ST.25/ascii requirements depends on filing date (e.g., ST.26 applies to applications filed on or after July 1, 2022); procedures determine whether a Sequence Listing XML must be submitted for a particular application (including provisional, PCT/national stage, and international filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes how to treat provisional applications, national stage PCT filings, and the timing implications for compliance with 37 CFR 1.831–1.835 and corresponding MPEP sections. Improper submissions under 1.821(c) are treated per the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Format for Sequence Listing under WIPO ST.25 (ASCII Plain Text CRF) (legacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications subject to WIPO ST.25 (legacy, pre-ST.26), a Sequence Listing may be submitted as ASCII plain text with a separate computer readable form (CRF); specific format and informational requirements apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ST.25 requirements include ASCII formatting rules, numeric identifiers, symbol conventions, provision of a CRF copy where required, and amendment procedures for adding or replacing Sequence Listings and CRFs under ST.25. Note: sections marked not applicable for apps filed on/after July 1, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Procedures; PatentIn and Checker Tools; Box SEQUENCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and recommended tools for preparing and submitting Sequence Listings: PatentIn software and a Checker are available; submission procedures include electronic upload and special handling for hand delivery (Box SEQUENCE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PatentIn (recommended) to reduce errors; Checker software helps identify compliance issues. For hand delivery, mark computer readable forms/read-only optical discs/papers 'Box SEQUENCE'; follow 37 CFR 1.52(e)(4) labeling. Do not hand-deliver extra electronic copies to examiners. Contact Patent Electronic Business Center or Sequence Systems Service Center for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of Patent Applications Claiming Large Numbers of Nucleotide Sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Polynucleotide molecules defined by their nucleic acid sequence that encode different proteins are normally considered independent and distinct inventions, and are presumptively subject to restriction under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent evidence to the contrary, each such nucleotide sequence is presumed independent; restriction/rejoinder and examination practice follow standards in MPEP §1850 and Examination of Patent Applications Containing Nucleotide Sequences guidance. Supplemental restriction requirements generally not advanced if merits action already made unless extenuating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing of Patents and Patent Application Publications with Lengthy Sequence Listings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Sequence Listing is lengthy (>= 600 KB, ~300 typed pages), it will not be printed in the paper/page-image version of the patent or publication; it will be published electronically (seqdata.uspto.gov) as an ASCII plain text file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized statements will appear in the page images to indicate where the Sequence Listing can be accessed. The USPTO forwards sequence data to NCBI; sequence data may be more easily searchable via NCBI. Applicants can request electronic copies (fees may apply). If the Sequence Listing is not in page images, a copy on electronic medium may be provided with mailed patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpful Hints and Common Errors for Sequence Rules Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tips to avoid common errors: remove non-ASCII characters, do not use tabs, ensure <130> or <140> present, update <160> if sequences changed, use proper scientific names in <213>, include mandatory feature for Unknown/Artificial sequences, use only standardized abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example specifics: spell out 'alpha' instead of non-ASCII symbols; do not use single letter amino acid abbreviations in the Sequence Listing; numeric identifier <213> must be 'Homo sapiens' rather than 'human'; when modifying Sequence Listings correct all similar errors, not just those listed in an error report. Contact Sequence Systems Service Center for specific processed-file issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation Rules for Special Molecular Situations (cyclic/branched peptides, unnatural residues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special molecular forms (cyclic peptides, branched peptides, peptides with D- or unnatural amino acids) have specific representation rules determining whether they fall under Sequence Listing rules or are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cyclic peptide with a tail is regarded as branched (and thereby exempt) if all bonds adjacent to the amino acid from which the tail emanates are normal peptide bonds. Presence of an unnatural amino acid does not have the same effect as presence of a D-amino acid; sequence may still be subject to the rules even with non-naturally occurring residues. Consult Sequence Systems Service Center for specific questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a Computer Readable Copy of the Sequence Listing
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer readable copy (CRF/ASCII/plain text or XML as applicable) of the Sequence Listing is required in addition to any textual presentation in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office requires a separate computer readable form for administrative processing and preservation of sequence data; CRF formatting and submission rules differ between ST.25 and ST.26. Do not rely solely on printed or image versions of the Sequence Listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions Regarding Compliance and Notifications for Failure to Comply
rubrics_metrics.description: There are regulatory presumptions regarding compliance with Sequence Listing requirements and formal notifications issued when Sequence Listing requirements are not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP describes presumptions and the issuance of a Notice relating to the requirements for applications containing sequence disclosures. Applicants must address notices (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.835) by filing appropriate amendments or Sequence Listing XML files; failure to comply may result in rejection or other prosecution consequences.
